text:
alice: Heads-up — seeing gRPC streaming stalls for model-serving traffic (pod->pod and node->node) in us-west-2.
Details: streaming requests (server-side streaming) hang after ~1–2MB of payload, client-side shows no more data, connection still ESTABLISHED. This started ~08:10 UTC after the big batch of node upgrades.

ben: Can you paste a tcpdump and MTU/interface output? :eyes:

alice: tcpdump (captured on node-a toward node-b):
```
15:23:45.123456 IP 10.10.5.12.36624 > 10.10.8.21.50051: Flags [P.], seq 1:1537, ack 1, win 29200, length 1536
15:23:45.123789 IP 10.10.5.12.36624 > 10.10.8.21.50051: Flags [.], ack 1, win 29200, length 0
15:23:46.223000 IP 10.10.5.12 > 10.10.8.21: ICMP 10.10.8.21 unreachable - need to frag (frag needed) mtu 1450
```
so we see ICMP frag-needed for some packets. gRPC stream client shows stall right after that packet. Server logs show repeated write attempts.

alice: ip link / routes:
```
# on node-a
ip link show vxlan0: mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state UP
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff
# on node-b
ip link show vxlan0: mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UP
```
node-a has vxlan MTU 1500 (older nodes), node-b 1450 (newer nodes). Physical NICs are jumbo (9000) on both but CNI set the tunnel differently during recent upgrades.

chloe: aha — MTU mismatch on overlay. If tunnel MTU is smaller and DF bit is set, you'll see PMTU ICMP frag-needed. Does kernel show GSO/TSO offload usage? Can you run `ethtool -k` on interfaces and check sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing?

alice: ethtool output (snip):
```
features for vxlan0:
  tx-gso: on
  tx-tso: on
  tx-ufo: off
```
sysctl: `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing = 0`

ben: Two attack vectors here:
- Mixed MTU across overlay means some flows will hit PMTU and rely on ICMP which can be rate-limited/blocked -> blackhole/stall.
- Offloads + GSO/TSO can produce large skbs that the overlay or switch can't handle and cause stalls for streaming large contiguous writes (like gRPC chunking).

dmitri: Quick mitigation: enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 cluster-wide and clamp MSS for TCP connections via CNI iptables CLAMP_MSS. Longer term need consistent tunnel MTU and uniform offload config.

alice: Confirmed: `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on node-a temporarily unblocks the stream. Client resumes and completes the stream. :relieved:

chloe: Also recommend adding an init hook in the CNI config to set `eth0`/`vxlan0` mtu to a controlled value (e.g., 1450) during node bootstrap and explicitly disable/enable offloads on older nodes to match fleet.

dmitri: Plan:
- patch: CNI to clamp MSS and set tunnel MTU to 1450 (PR ready) :shipit:
- rolling restart of CNI on all nodes (no pod evictions if possible) starting 02:00 UTC
- kubelet/OS image patch to normalize ethtool offload settings (tx-gso/tx-tso) per NodeProfile
- add an alert for ICMP frag-needed spikes in netflow

ben: Also add a postmortem note: why the node upgrade pipeline didn't enforce tunnel MTU parity. Cost risk: cross-AZ transfers spike when fragmentation happens.

infra-bot: ALERT: packet_loss_rate_threshold exceeded on us-west-2 between node-a/node-b 08:11 UTC — triggered automated-scrape. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/networking/pmtu

alice: Thanks — will monitor after the CNI rollout. Will post perf numbers and tcpdump before/after. :+1:

chloe: TL;DR: MTU mismatch + GSO/TSO interplay caused large-packet fragmentation and ICMP PMTU dependence, which led to gRPC streaming stalls. Fix = normalize tunnel MTU + MSS clamp + enable probing as fallback.

ben: Nice investigation, Alice. Please include the minimal repro steps so SRE can run a canary across AZs.

alice: Will do. Repro steps (short):
1) create two nodes with vxlan MTU mismatch (1500 vs 1450)
2) deploy simple gRPC server that streams ~5MB in 512KB chunks
3) curl/grpc client observe stall after ~1–2MB unless tcp_mtu_probing=1 or MSS clamped
